Visualization

IFU Analyzer provides powerful visualization tools to explore and display your data effectively. Learn how to customize the appearance and interact with your data.

Display Options

Intensity Map Display

The main intensity map shows a 2D projection of your 3D data cube:

  • Each pixel represents a spatial location (spaxel)

  • Color shows intensity at the current wavelength

  • Interactive: Click any location to update the spectrum

Spectrum Panel Display

The spectrum panel shows 1D data:

  • X-axis: Wavelength or frequency

  • Y-axis: Intensity (flux or count rate)

  • Mouse hover: Show exact values

  • Right-click: Detailed spectrum options

Color Scales

Different color scales emphasize different aspects of your data:

Linear Scale (Default)

  • Direct mapping: intensity → color

  • Best for: Data without extreme value ranges

  • Fast computation

Logarithmic Scale

  • Scale: intensity → log(intensity)

  • Best for: Wide dynamic range

  • Emphasizes: Faint features

  • How to enable: View → Color Scale → Logarithmic

Power Law Scale

  • Scale: intensity → intensity^power

  • Adjustable exponent (0.5 to 2.0)

  • Best for: Custom emphasis

  • How to enable: View → Color Scale → Power

Square Root Scale

  • Scale: intensity → √intensity

  • Best for: Moderate dynamic range

  • Balanced detail emphasis

Choosing Color Scale

Use this guide:

Data Type

Best Scale

Continuum

Linear (nice gradients)

Narrow Lines

Logarithmic (show faint wings)

Stars

Square Root (emphasize core without overwhelming)

Weak Features

Logarithmic or Power

Residuals

Linear (equal weight to all deviations)

To change scale:

  1. Click Color Scale button in toolbar

  2. Select desired scale

  3. Adjust parameters interactively if offered

  4. View updates in real-time

Intensity Range (vmin/vmax)

Histogram Stretch

Manually set the intensity range displayed:

  1. Click Intensity Range panel

  2. Adjust vmin (minimum displayed intensity)

  3. Adjust vmax (maximum displayed intensity)

  4. Clipped values appear as black (below vmin) or white (above vmax)

Auto-Scale

Automatically set optimal range:

  • Button: Auto Scale (shows in intensity range panel)

  • Resets to 1st and 99th percentile of data

  • Useful after dramatic region changes

Percentile Stretch

Set range based on percentiles:

  1. Open Color Scale dialog

  2. Set min percentile (e.g., 5%)

  3. Set max percentile (e.g., 95%)

  4. Automatically clips outliers

Full Range

Show all data without clipping:

  • Click Full Range button

  • Reveals entire data range

  • May reduce contrast if outliers present

Colormaps

Colormaps control how intensity is mapped to colors. IFU Analyzer includes many options:

Built-in Colormaps

Name

Usage

Viridis

Default, most perceptually uniform, good for presentations

Hot

Red/yellow/white, good for thermal data

Cool

Cyan/blue, good for cool/absorbed regions

RdYlBu

Red-yellow-blue diverging, good for positive/negative data

Binary

Black to white, good for monochrome presentations

Inferno

High contrast, good for dramatic effects

Plasma

Perceptually uniform alternative to Viridis

Grey

Grayscale, good for printing

Changing Colormaps

  1. Click Colormap button in toolbar

  2. Select colormap from list

  3. Preview updates immediately

  4. Some support Invert option for reversed color order

Custom Colormaps

Advanced users can define custom colormaps:

  1. Tools → Preferences → Color Management

  2. Load custom colormap file

  3. Or create in external tool (Matplotlib)

Colormap Best Practices

  • Scientific papers: Use uniform colormaps (Viridis, Inferno)

  • Presentations: Use contrasting colormaps (Hot, Cool)

  • Printing: Use colormaps that work in grayscale

  • Colorblind: Avoid pure red-green combinations

Zoom Controls

Zooming In/Out

Zoom Levels

  • 1:1 = 100% (one data pixel = one screen pixel)

  • 1:2 = 50% (one data pixel = half screen)

  • 2:1 = 200% (one data pixel = two screen)

Pan View

Move around zoomed view:

  • Middle mouse button + drag

  • Or hold Spacebar + drag

  • Arrow keys for precise movement

Fit to Window

Automatically scale view:

  • Use the Reset View button in the toolbar

  • Resets pan and zoom

Reset View

Return to default view using the Reset View button in the toolbar.

Overlays

Grid Overlay

Shows coordinate grid:

  • View → Show Grid

  • Adjustable color and spacing

  • Useful for measuring positions

Measurement Tools

Add measurement annotations:

  • Right-click map → Add Measurement

  • Distance measurements

  • Angle measurements

  • Area measurements

Region Outlines

Selected regions display outlines:

  • Rectangle: Green outline

  • Circle: Blue outline

  • Custom: Yellow outline

  • Color customizable in preferences

Coordinate Display

Current cursor position shows:

  • RA/DEC coordinates (if WCS available)

  • Pixel coordinates (always available)

  • Wavelength/Velocity

  • Intensity value

Spectral Overlay

When fitting, overlay shows:

  • Fitted Gaussian curve (red)

  • Baseline (yellow)

  • Residuals (green shaded)

  • Chi-squared value

Exporting Visualizations

Save Current View as Image

  1. File → Export Visualization

  2. Choose format (PNG, JPEG, PDF)

  3. Specify filename

  4. Click Export

High-Resolution Export

For publication-quality figures:

  1. File → Export Visualization

  2. Choose High Resolution

  3. Select up to 4× magnification

  4. Export as PDF or PNG

Batch Export

Export multiple wavelengths as images:

  1. File → Batch Export

  2. Specify wavelength range

  3. Choose step size

  4. Select output directory

  5. Click Start

Animation/Movies

Create animated sequences:

  1. File → Create Animation

  2. Set wavelength range

  3. Set frame rate (number of channels per second)

  4. Choose output format (GIF, MP4, WebM)

  5. Click Create

Useful for:

  • Presentations

  • Publications

  • Data exploration

  • Communicating results to collaborators

Display Performance

For smooth performance with large cubes:

Enable Display Decimation

  • Tools → Preferences → Performance

  • When enabled, skips pixels for speed

  • Toggle with P key while viewing

Resolution Adjustment

  • Reduce display resolution temporarily

  • Tools → Display Resolution

  • Choose 50%, 33%, or 25% of full resolution

Memory Management

  • Monitor memory usage (status bar)

  • Close other applications if needed

  • Use downsampled cubes for initial exploration

Troubleshooting Visualization

Colors look washed out

  • Adjust vmin/vmax

  • Try different color scale

  • Check display monitor gamma

Very pixelated appearance

  • Zoom in with scroll wheel

  • Use View → Fit to Window

  • Enable smoothing interpolation

Slow performance

  • Enable Display Decimation

  • Reduce display resolution

  • Close other applications

  • Consider downsampling cube

Colors don’t match expectations

  • Verify wavelength selection

  • Check color scale type

  • Confirm data is calibrated

  • Try different colormap
